name: Nethander Stead
summary: Along the road east of Southshore, Nethander Stead lies abandoned beneath the Mudsnout gnolls. Giant white Mudsnout Blossoms now cover its fields and draw Forsaken alchemists.

sections.title: A Ruined Homestead
sections.body: Ruined fences and outbuildings at Nethander Stead stand within sight of Southshore’s eastern borders. Once part of Hillsbrad’s working fields, the farm was abandoned as security weakened and wild packs moved in. The Mudsnout gnolls make their only home in these foothills. They drive off travelers who come too close to their territory.

sections.title: The Mudsnout Blossoms
sections.body: Giant, pale mushrooms called Mudsnout Blossoms cover the farm’s untended plots. Their natural toxins are potent, and the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill seeks samples. Its apothecaries use the gnolls’ ground to gather them for caustic mixtures. Covert Horde parties enter Alliance territory to bring back the blossoms.

faq.answer: Along the road just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Nethander Stead is an abandoned human farm. Mudsnout gnolls have overrun it.

faq.q: Who controls Nethander Stead right now?
faq.answer: The Mudsnout gnolls occupy the farmstead. It is the only place in the Hillsbrad Foothills where this pack makes camp.

faq.q: What are the giant white mushrooms growing in the fields?
faq.answer: The giant white mushrooms are Mudsnout Blossoms, growing in the farm’s unworked soil. Their toxic properties make them valuable to Forsaken alchemists studying poisons.

faq.q: Why does the Horde care about this ruined farm?
faq.answer: Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks Mudsnout Blossoms from the farm’s fields. Their potent juices are essential to making the Elixir of Agony.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you can see how fragile Southshore’s perimeter remains in the gnolls entrenched just down the eastern road.
As a member of the Horde, you can gather Mudsnout Blossoms at this farmstead near Southshore for the Royal Apothecary Society’s lethal research.
